title: Building Degree-Linked Apprenticeships with Education Partners
description: For boards that want to move from referring to building. Covers convening an employer, a college, and a sponsor; aligning work processes with course outcomes; credit articulation; and funding the build through CAI, AIF, Regional Coordination Project funds (WSIN25-21), and WIOA.
notes: Audience: Board staff, business services leads, community college and adult school partners. Format: HD. Hours assumed from format (HD = 4 hours). Track note: California's apprenticeship-degree landscape is early. AB 1904 (credentialed educator apprenticeships) and the Chancellor's Office Apprenticeship Pathway Demonstration Project are the anchors; a CSU or Apprenticeship Degree Network footprint was not verified. These courses should be refreshed as the field develops.
learning_objectives: Identify the partners and roles needed for a degree-linked apprenticeship.
Crosswalk an apprenticeship's work processes to course learning outcomes.
Draft a funding plan for program development.
Write the partnership language for a local plan modification or grant application.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Assembling the Partnership; Crosswalking Work Processes to Course Outcomes; Funding the Build; Writing Partnership Language. The closing project ("Project: Draft a Degree-Linked Apprenticeship Proposal") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a degree-linked apprenticeship proposal with a partner map, work-process crosswalk, funding plan, and partnership language) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (HD; HD = 4 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Track caveat: California's apprenticeship-degree landscape is early. AB 1904 (credentialed educator apprenticeships) and the Chancellor's Office Apprenticeship Pathway Demonstration Project are the anchors; a CSU or Apprenticeship Degree Network footprint was not verified. These courses should be refreshed as the field develops. Prerequisites reflect track order: DEG 101 (Apprenticeship Degrees); APP 103 (Braiding the Money) recommended.
